label: defect

source.note: 1. AC5 has no snapshot point for a killed session. The plan says what each reader reports and computes wall time as 'now - previous row'. It never says which process takes the snapshot for a session killed mid-turn. A killed session makes no further transition, and no Stop hook fires on a kill. SweepLateDriverUsage is keyed to the current session id, so a new session that later engages or steals the seat cannot recover the dead session's usage. acquireEngagementLease already has a stale-seat path, lease.OutcomeStolen, and the plan does not hook it. Wall time measured at a later detection would also run up to that detection, not to the kill. The plan must name the trigger, for example a seat steal or reap, or a sweep across all sessions with an open driver window. It must also say what bounds the wall time, such as the lease heartbeat or the last timestamp in the record. 2. The rules for AC5 and AC7 contradict each other on a repeated identical cumulative. [...] 3. AC6 late rows depend on the same session calling satelle again. [...] 4. AC4 has no workable way to update rows on an append-only ledger. [...]

summary: Frozen from the real plan-review reject on sty_81caa41b, attempt 1 (2026-09-27, evt_716d5343). change.diff is trimmed to finding 1 of 4 -- the AC5 section as submitted, which names no snapshot trigger and no wall-time bound for a session killed mid-turn. The other three findings are preserved verbatim in source.note but not separately diffed, to keep the fixture small (see tests/reviewcorpus README, Provenance).
